ip_blocked.label: Sending IP blocked
ip_blocked.description: The sending server's IP is on a block list. Request delisting at the listing service (the authority) and review what triggered it.

rate_limited.label: Rate limited
rate_limited.description: The recipient domain is throttling mail from this IP. Lower the sending rate and concurrency, then retry later.

auth_failure.label: Sender authentication failed
auth_failure.description: SPF, DKIM, DMARC or reverse DNS checks failed. Review the sending domain's DNS records and the sending server's configuration.

sender_blocked.label: Sender address rejected
sender_blocked.description: The recipient domain rejects mail from this sender address. Ask the recipient's administrator to unblock it, or change the sender address.

content_rejected.label: Content rejected
content_rejected.description: The body or an attachment was rejected as spam, a virus or by policy. Review the message content and attachments.

message_too_large.label: Message too large
message_too_large.description: The message exceeds the recipient's size limit. Reduce the attachments or share them another way.

server_config.label: Sending server misconfigured
server_config.description: Relay, TLS or HELO settings do not meet the recipient's requirements. Check the sending server (MTA) configuration.

dns_resolver_failure.label: DNS resolver failure (own server)
dns_resolver_failure.description: Your mail server could not look up the recipient's name in DNS, yet the name exists when MailCare looks it up. Check the server's name resolution (resolv.conf, the local caching resolver such as unbound, the upstream resolver, UDP and TCP port 53, DNSSEC validation).

unknown_failure.label: Unknown failure
unknown_failure.description: A delivery failure that matches no known pattern. Read the diagnostic and the source messages, and use the analysis report if needed.

dmarc_spf_missing.label: SPF record missing
dmarc_spf_missing.description: Mail with this domain in From failed DMARC because the domain it was checked against (such as the sending server's host name) has no usable SPF record. If the source is a server of the domain, publish an SPF record and set up DKIM signing.

dmarc_dkim_failed.label: DKIM verification failed
dmarc_dkim_failed.description: Mail signed with this domain's DKIM key failed verification and DMARC. Either a forwarder on the receiving side changed the mail or the sending side's DKIM setup is wrong. Check the sending IPs.

dmarc_not_authenticated.label: Sender not authenticated
dmarc_not_authenticated.description: Mail with this domain in From came from sources with neither a DKIM signature of the domain nor SPF authorization, and failed DMARC. Check the sending IPs to tell a legitimate service missing from SPF from spoofing.

user_unknown.label: Recipient does not exist
user_unknown.description: The recipient address does not exist. Remove it from the list or ask the recipient for the correct address.

mailbox_full.label: Recipient mailbox full
mailbox_full.description: The recipient's mailbox is over quota. Nothing can be done on the sending side; mail arrives once they free space.

mailbox_disabled.label: Recipient address disabled
mailbox_disabled.description: The recipient address is disabled or suspended. Remove it from the list or ask the recipient for another address.

domain_not_found.label: Recipient domain not found
domain_not_found.description: The recipient domain has no DNS (MX) record. Check the spelling; otherwise wait for the recipient's DNS to recover.

dns_failure_external.label: DNS failure (receiving side or external)
dns_failure_external.description: A failed DNS lookup was reported, but when MailCare looks the recipient's name up again, the name exists, or the answers are inconsistent or the receiving side's name servers fail. The receiving side's DNS or another provider's resolver is at fault; nothing can be done on the sending side. Contact the recipient side only if it persists.

delivery_delay.label: Delivery delayed
delivery_delay.description: The recipient server is temporarily unreachable. Mail is retried automatically; contact the recipient side only if it persists.

mailbox.addressHint: The address to monitor. It is stored in lower case.
mailbox.enabledHint: When disabled, the mailbox is skipped by scheduled syncs.
mailbox.initialDaysHint: Days to look back on the first sync (default 90)
mailbox.recentDaysHint: Days to look back on later syncs (default 10)
mailbox.serverKeepDaysHint: Bounces and other notices, and junk mails, older than this many days (from the mail's date) are deleted from the server. 0 never deletes them on the server. Deletion on the server cannot be undone, and junk detection can be wrong: for an address that receives mail you must keep by law or policy (such as records of electronic transactions), set 0 or archive the mail first.
mailbox.serverKeepDaysMax: At most the mail retention of the general settings ({{max}} days).
mailbox.smtpHostHint: The host name of the SMTP server that sends the mail of this address (e.g. mail.example.jp; optional), written as the server calls itself: the name in the "by ..." part of the Received headers it adds and in "This is the mail system at host ..." of its notices. The probe mails are sent through this server. It is also used to recognize the delivery-failure notices this server issued and the notices about mail that was not sent from the sending servers; without it (and without a host name in the general settings) the latter are not recognized for this address. The IPv4 / IPv6 addresses of the name are looked up automatically; registering the server's IP addresses in "Sending servers" of the general settings as well is the safe choice. To apply a change to the mail already fetched, run "Reclassify" on the Tools screen.

setting.checkTimesHint: All enabled mailboxes are synced automatically at these times.
setting.mailKeepDaysHint: Mails older than this many days, counted from their date, are removed by the daily cleanup. The bounce groups they belonged to are recounted; a group left without mails is removed together with its analysis report.
setting.cleanupTimeHint: Every day at this time, the mails, workspaces and other data past their retention are removed (it can also be started from the Tools page).
setting.workersHint: Number of jobs that run at the same time. Accounts on the same IMAP server are processed one after another automatically.
setting.agentModelExamples: Models you can use (click to fill in)
setting.agentModelUnsupported: This provider does not support choosing a model.
setting.agentReasoningUnsupported: This provider does not support choosing a reasoning level.
setting.agentEnabledHint: When enabled, new bounces found by a sync are analyzed automatically.
setting.agentKeepDaysHint: How many days the workspace directory of each analysis run (prompt, CLI output, report) is kept. Older ones are removed by the daily cleanup.
setting.recheckDaysHint: After a group is marked resolved, a notice about mail sent after this many days marks it "Resolved (re)". Notices before that are taken as arriving while a delisting or another change takes effect.
setting.ownSendingHint: The servers that send your organization's mail: the "SMTP server (sending)" of each mail address together with what is registered here. Register here the sources not tied to a mail address (an application that delivers directly to the recipients' servers, another relay, an external delivery service and so on). A bounce (a notice that mail could not be delivered) that was not issued by one of your own mail servers and whose original mail passed through none of your own sending servers is taken as a notice about mail someone else sent with your organization's address forged as the sender, and is treated as junk. This judgement is made for each mail address separately, only while a host name is known for it: its own SMTP server, or a host name registered here, which counts for every address (a server appears in the headers of the mail it handles by its name, so IP addresses alone are not enough). The servers also tell whether a notice about a failed DNS lookup came from your own mail server (for an address with no server known, neither here nor its own SMTP server, every such notice is taken as coming from your own mail server). The IPv4 / IPv6 addresses of the host names are looked up automatically and compared as well. While the DNS check is on, the SPF record of the domain of each mail address is read too, and the sending addresses it lists count as your own. Warning: bounces of mail sent through a route outside your own sending servers (an external delivery service, another server, a separate mailing application and so on) are treated as junk and do not appear as alerts unless the mail is signed (DKIM) with your organization's domain. After changing the servers, run "Reclassify" on the Tools screen to apply them to the mail already fetched. Enter one per line, up to {{max}} per list.
setting.ownSendingIpv4Hint: IPv4 addresses or CIDRs. Register the addresses of the machines that actually connect to the recipients' mail servers: your SMTP server's own sending address, and any application that delivers directly without going through the SMTP server. Applications and devices that only hand their mail to your SMTP server need not be listed.
setting.ownSendingIpv6Hint: IPv6 addresses or CIDRs. Register the addresses of the machines that actually connect to the recipients' mail servers: your SMTP server's own sending address, and any application that delivers directly without going through the SMTP server. Applications and devices that only hand their mail to your SMTP server need not be listed.
setting.ownSendingHostsHint: Host names of sending servers not tied to a mail address (the SMTP server of a mail address is entered in the settings of that address). Enter the name each server calls itself: the one in the "by ..." part of the Received headers it adds and in "This is the mail system at host ..." of its notices. The names are compared as written with the route of the original mail and with the server that issued the notice, and their IPv4 / IPv6 addresses are looked up automatically and compared too. As a server may also appear under another name, registering its IP addresses as well is the safe choice. Short names without a domain (such as mailhost) are accepted. To apply a change to the mail already fetched, run "Reclassify" on the Tools screen.
setting.ownSendingMailboxHosts: SMTP servers of the mail addresses
setting.ownSendingMailboxHostsHint: The "SMTP server (sending)" entered in the settings of each mail address. Each one switches the judgement of notices about mail not sent from your servers on for its own address only; all of them are recognized as your own servers for every address. They are changed in the settings of each mail address.
setting.dnsCheckEnabledHint: On by default. When a notice says a name could not be looked up, the name is looked up again to tell whether the recipient domain does not exist or the resolver of the reporting server is failing. MailCare then asks the resolvers below for the names in notices and the MX, NS and SPF records of the domains concerned; the name servers of the domain are asked directly only for notices about your own mail. The host names of your own sending servers are looked up through the OS resolver first, and asked of the resolvers below only when it returns no address (short names without a domain are looked up through the OS resolver only). The SPF records of the domains of your mail addresses are read too, and the sending addresses they list count as your own. Turning it off stops every query except looking up the host names of your own sending servers through the OS resolver. See "Outbound connections" in the README.
setting.dnsCheckResolversHint: The DNS resolvers asked. One IPv4 or IPv6 address per line, up to {{max}} (default: Cloudflare 1.1.1.1, Google 8.8.8.8 and Quad9 9.9.9.9). The queries are plain, unencrypted DNS (port 53): the resolvers and the networks on the way see this server's IP address and the names asked.
setting.dnsCheckSystemResolverOnlyHint: Asks only the resolver set up in the server's OS instead of the ones above, and no name server directly. The OS resolver often belongs to the same setup as your mail servers, so it is a weaker independent check; and with a single resolver, differences between public resolvers cannot be detected.

tools.description: Run fetch, grouping and analysis separately or together, rebuild the index, redo the classification, or apply the retentions with a cleanup.
tools.allNote: With "All", one job is expanded per mailbox and they run in parallel within the worker limit.

sync.title: Sync all (fetch, group, analyze)
sync.description: Fetches mail, groups new bounces and analyzes the actionable groups. The same processing as a scheduled sync.

fetch.title: Fetch only
fetch.description: Stores mail not yet fetched from the IMAP server. No grouping or analysis.

group.title: Group only
group.description: Classifies fetched mail that is awaiting grouping, groups it and analyzes the groups awaiting analysis.

analyze.title: Analyze only
analyze.description: Runs the agent analysis, either for groups awaiting analysis or for every actionable group.

reindex.title: Reindex
reindex.description: Rebuilds the index database and re-parses, re-classifies and re-groups every stored raw message.
reindex.warning: This takes a while. Group states and analysis reports are kept only for groups that appear again.

reclassify.title: Reclassify
reclassify.description: Keeps the messages and re-runs only bounce classification and grouping. Use after classification rules change.

cleanup.title: Cleanup
cleanup.description: Deletes the bounces and other notices past the retention of their mail address (except those recognized by subject or sender name alone, and automatically generated messages) and the junk mails from the IMAP server, then removes the mails past the mail retention (original, body sections and index row), the temporary files left by interrupted writes, the old agent workspaces and the jobs finished more than 30 days ago. The server runs this automatically every day at the cleanup time.
cleanup.warning: Mails deleted from the IMAP server cannot be restored. A bounce group left without mails is removed together with its analysis report.

jobs.description: Background processing such as fetching, grouping and analysis. Active jobs refresh automatically. Jobs queued for "All" appear as one child job per mailbox.

notifications.settingsHint: When and to whom notification mails are sent.
notifications.sendNowHint: Sends the notification mail with the saved settings without waiting for the notification time.
notifications.sendBlocked: The saved settings do not allow sending. See the notice above.

tokens.description: Tokens are reserved for the future API and are not used for the web login.
tokens.futureNote: When no token exists, the server creates a "default" token by itself.
tokens.createdOnce: This value is shown only once. Store it somewhere safe.

profile.profileHint: Change your display name, notification address, language, time zone and theme.
profile.emailHint: Recipient of notification mails. When an administrator selects you as a recipient, the alert digest arrives here. It can also be used to log in. Leave empty to clear.
profile.changePasswordHint: Confirm your current password, then set a new one.
profile.sessionNote: Changing the password logs out every other device.

probeSettings.description: Every mail address sends probe mails to the probe server, and their arrival is checked, so delays and failures of mail are noticed.
probeSettings.serverHint: How to reach the mailbox that receives the probe mails. The probe mails whose arrival is confirmed are deleted from it to free space (the account must be allowed to delete mail). Use a mailbox reserved for the probe. The password is stored encrypted.
probeSettings.scheduleHint: The send times and the thresholds of delays and failures. When the next send time comes, the probe mails not arrived yet are looked for by the new arrival check as well.
probeSettings.noSendTimes: No send time: probe mails are not sent automatically.
probeSettings.testSaveFirst: The connection test uses the values being edited.
probeSettings.noMailboxes: No enabled mail address has a sending server (SMTP). Set the "Sending server" of each address under "Mail addresses".
probeSettings.notifyHint: Failures are mailed to the notification recipients through the SMTP server of "Notifications" (whether the notification mail is on or off).

status.notConfigured: Set the probe address and the connection of the probe server (host, username, password) to switch it on.

probes.description: The arrival of the probe mails sent from every mail address to the probe server.
probes.recentHint: Recovered and resolved count the last {{days}} days.
probes.mailboxes: Latest probe mail per mail address
probes.disabled: No probe mail is sent and no arrival is checked.
probes.notConfiguredTitle: The delivery probe is not set up
probes.notConfigured: Set the probe server and the probe address to watch for delays and failures of mail.
probes.checkError: The probe server could not be read ({{error}}). It is tried again shortly.
probes.checkErrorMember: The probe server could not be read. It is tried again shortly.
probes.resolveHint: Marks it resolved without waiting for its arrival. That it was delayed or failed is kept.

empty.issues: No probe mail was delayed or failed
